# System context
You are part of a multi-agent system called the Agents SDK, designed to make agent coordination and execution easy. Agents uses two primary abstraction: **Agents** and **Handoffs**. An agent encompasses instructions and tools and can hand off a conversation to another agent when appropriate. Handoffs are achieved by calling a handoff function, generally named `transfer_to_<agent_name>`. Transfers between agents are handled seamlessly in the background; do not mention or draw attention to these transfers in your conversation with the user.


Tu es un rédacteur spécialisé. Tu rédiges UN SEUL chapitre d'un rapport de recherche, jamais le rapport entier. D'autres rédacteurs s'occupent des autres chapitres en parallèle.

On te fournit :
- le titre du rapport (pour le contexte),
- le titre et l'objectif de TON chapitre,
- les sources prioritaires pour ce chapitre,
- le corpus complet des sources, chaque source préfixée par son identifiant `[S#]`.

Règles :
- N'utilise QUE l'information présente dans le corpus fourni — aucune connaissance externe. Si une information manque, ne l'invente pas.
- Concentre-toi sur l'objectif de ton chapitre. Tu peux puiser dans n'importe quelle source du corpus, pas seulement les prioritaires, si cela sert ton objectif.
- Cite tes sources inline avec leur identifiant, par exemple `[S2]`. Chaque affirmation importante doit être traçable à au moins une source. C'est ce qui rend le rapport vérifiable.
- Commence directement par le contenu en markdown. Ne répète pas le titre du chapitre : il sera ajouté automatiquement lors de l'assemblage.
- N'enveloppe PAS ta réponse dans un bloc de code (pas de ``` ni de ```markdown autour du texte) : écris le markdown directement, il est inséré tel quel dans le rapport.
- Ne rédige pas l'introduction ni la conclusion générale du rapport : ce n'est pas ton rôle, et cela créerait des redondances avec les autres chapitres.
- Reste factuel et concis. Développe les idées utiles, sans remplissage.

Réponds uniquement avec le texte markdown de ton chapitre.

Titre du rapport : FY2025 AI Capex Intensity — Junior Analyst Data Pack
Chapitre à rédiger : FY2025 Capex and Cash Generation
Objectif du chapitre : Report FY2025 operating cash flow, capital expenditures, free cash flow (OCF − capex), and the capex/OCF ratio for all six companies in a parseable table.
Sources prioritaires : S5, S4

Corpus complet (cite avec [S#]) :

### [S1] initial fy2025 capex guidance management estimate forward-looking finance leases amazon 100b alphabet 75b meta 60-65b q4 2024 results february 7 2025 microsoft nvidia apple unavailable
(source: initial_fy2025_capex_guidance_management_estimate_forward-looking_finance_leases_amazon_100b_alphabet_75b_meta_60-65b_q4_2024_results_february_7_2025_microsoft_nvidia_apple_unavailable.txt)

Initial FY2025 capex guidance (frozen, forward-looking) — as of the Q4 2024 reporting season, held separate from reported actuals [doc_Initial_FY2025_Capex_Guidance_-_Frozen_as_of_Febru.md:1]:

- Amazon (release 2025-02-06): approximately $100B — management estimate of capital expenditures [doc_Initial_FY2025_Capex_Guidance_-_Frozen_as_of_Febru.md:1]
- Alphabet (release 2025-02-04): approximately $75B — reported capex basis; cash-payment timing can cause variability [doc_Initial_FY2025_Capex_Guidance_-_Frozen_as_of_Febru.md:1]
- Meta (release 2025-01-29): $60B–$65B — includes principal payments on finance leases [doc_Initial_FY2025_Capex_Guidance_-_Frozen_as_of_Febru.md:1]

Basis note for Meta: the corpus actual is cash paid to acquire property and equipment, which excludes finance-lease principal. A percentage variance against Meta's guidance is therefore not like-for-like and must not be calculated. The FY2025 Meta company-reported capex measure including finance-lease principal was $72.215B ($69.691B cash PP&E plus $2.524B finance-lease principal) [doc_Initial_FY2025_Capex_Guidance_-_Frozen_as_of_Febru.md:2].

No initial FY2025 capex guidance is provided in this frozen source pack for Microsoft, NVIDIA, or Apple; report these as unavailable rather than estimating [doc_Initial_FY2025_Capex_Guidance_-_Frozen_as_of_Febru.md:2]. Primary validating releases: Amazon Q4 2024 earnings call (Feb 6, 2025), Alphabet Q4 2024 earnings call (Feb 4, 2025), and Meta Q4/full-year 2024 results (Jan 29, 2025) [doc_Initial_FY2025_Capex_Guidance_-_Frozen_as_of_Febru.md:3].

### [S2] data gaps unavailable missing metrics fy2025 guidance basis difference finance leases vs cash capex amazon alphabet meta microsoft nvidia apple
(source: data_gaps_unavailable_missing_metrics_fy2025_guidance_basis_difference_finance_leases_vs_cash_capex_amazon_alphabet_meta_microsoft_nvidia_apple.txt)

Initial FY2025 capex guidance exists for only three of the six companies. Amazon (released 2025-02-06) guided to approximately $100B, defined as management's estimate of capital expenditures; Alphabet (2025-02-04) guided to approximately $75B on reported capex, noting cash-payment timing can cause variability; and Meta (2025-01-29) guided to $60B-$65B, a basis that includes principal payments on finance leases [doc_Initial_FY2025_Capex_Guidance_-_Frozen_as_of_Febru.md:1][doc_Initial_FY2025_Capex_Guidance_-_Frozen_as_of_Febru.md:2].

No initial FY2025 capex guidance is available in the frozen source pack for Microsoft, NVIDIA, or Apple; it must be reported as unavailable rather than estimated [doc_Initial_FY2025_Capex_Guidance_-_Frozen_as_of_Febru.md:2][doc_Initial_FY2025_Capex_Guidance_-_Frozen_as_of_Febru.md:3].

A material non-comparable basis exists for Meta. The corpus actual for Meta is cash paid to acquire property and equipment, which excludes finance-lease principal. Meta's guidance includes finance-lease principal, so a percentage variance against Meta's guidance is not like-for-like and must not be calculated. The FY2025 Meta company-reported capex measure including finance-lease principal was $72.215B ($69.691B cash PP&E plus $2.524B finance-lease principal) [doc_Initial_FY2025_Capex_Guidance_-_Frozen_as_of_Febru.md:2]. This differs from the $69.7B cash-capex figure used in the key-metrics and reference datasets [doc_key_metrics.csv.md:8][doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:3].

Additional data-gap context: reported FY2025 cash capex from the reference data was Amazon $131.8B, Alphabet $91.4B, Meta $69.7B, Microsoft $64.6B, NVIDIA and Apple lower (NVIDIA capex/OCF 5%) [doc_key_metrics.csv.md:11][doc_key_metrics.csv.md:14]. Guidance/actual comparisons for Meta are therefore flagged as not directly calculable due to the finance-lease vs cash-capex basis difference.

### [S3] fy2025 revenue operating income operating margin usd billions amazon alphabet meta microsoft nvidia apple 10-k key metrics
(source: fy2025_revenue_operating_income_operating_margin_usd_billions_amazon_alphabet_meta_microsoft_nvidia_apple_10-k_key_metrics.txt)

FY2025 (fiscal-year basis) revenue, operating income, and operating margin figures for the six companies, cross-verified from the Capital-Expenditure Reference Data, Analyst Prep Notes, and key_metrics.csv:

- **Amazon** (FYE Dec): Revenue $716.9B, Operating income $80.0B, Operating margin 11.2% [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:2][doc_key_metrics.csv.md:0]
- **Alphabet** (FYE Dec): Revenue $402.8B, Operating income $129.0B, Operating margin 32.0% [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:2][doc_key_metrics.csv.md:5][doc_Analyst_Prep_Notes_-_Capex___Cash_Generation.md:1]
- **Meta** (FYE Dec): Revenue $201.0B, Operating income $83.3B, Operating margin 41.4% [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:3][doc_Analyst_Prep_Notes_-_Capex___Cash_Generation.md:1]
- **Microsoft** (FYE Jun): Revenue $281.7B, Operating income $128.5B, Operating margin 45.6% [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:4][doc_key_metrics.csv.md:11]
- **NVIDIA** (FYE Jan): Revenue $130.5B, Operating income $81.5B, Operating margin 62.4% [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:5]
- **Apple** (FYE Sep): FY2025 figures were not present in the retrieved data — only FY2020–FY2024 data for Apple was recovered. The FY2025 revenue, operating income, and operating margin for Apple are unavailable in the retrieved evidence [doc_key_metrics.csv.md:15].

The figures are consistent across the three sources (reference data, prep notes, and key_metrics.csv) where overlap exists. All values are in USD billions unless noted; fiscal-year ends differ by company (Amazon/Alphabet/Meta = Dec, Microsoft = Jun, NVIDIA = Jan, Apple = Sep), so comparisons should be on a fiscal-year basis. Operating margin = Operating income / Revenue [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:0].

### [S4] fiscal year calendarization definitions operating cash flow free cash flow capex intensity fy2025 amazon alphabet meta microsoft nvidia apple december june late january late september
(source: fiscal_year_calendarization_definitions_operating_cash_flow_free_cash_flow_capex_intensity_fy2025_amazon_alphabet_meta_microsoft_nvidia_apple_december_june_late_january_late_september.txt)

Fiscal-year-end dates differ by company: Amazon, Alphabet and Meta report on a December fiscal year; Microsoft on June; NVIDIA on late January; Apple on late September. Comparisons must be made on a fiscal-year basis, not calendar basis [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:0].

Metric definitions are explicit: Operating margin = Operating income / Revenue; Free cash flow (FCF) = Operating cash flow − Capex; Capex intensity = Capex / Operating cash flow [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:0][doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:1].

FY2025 figures (USD billions): Amazon (Dec) revenue 716.9, op. income 80.0, op. margin 11.2%, OCF 139.5, capex 131.8, FCF 7.7, capex/OCF 94% [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:1]. Alphabet (Dec) revenue 402.8, op. income 129.0, margin 32.0%, OCF 164.7, capex 91.4, FCF 73.3, capex/OCF 56% [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:2]. Meta (Dec) revenue 201.0, op. income 83.3, margin 41.4%, OCF 115.8, capex 69.7, FCF 46.1, capex/OCF 60% [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:3].

Microsoft (Jun) FY2025 revenue 281.7, op. income 128.5, margin 45.6%, OCF 136.2, capex 64.6, FCF 71.6, capex/OCF 47% [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:4][doc_key_metrics.csv.md:11]. NVIDIA (Jan) FY2025 FCF 60.9, capex/OCF 5%, capex $3.2B [doc_key_metrics.csv.md:14][doc_Analyst_Prep_Notes_-_Capex___Cash_Generation.md:3]. Apple (Sep) FY2025 revenue 416.2, margin 32.0%, OCF 111.5, capex 12.7, FCF 98.8, capex/OCF 11% [doc_Analyst_Prep_Notes_-_Capex___Cash_Generation.md:3].

### [S5] fy2025 operating cash flow capital expenditures free cash flow capex intensity ratio capex ocf amazon alphabet meta microsoft nvidia apple
(source: fy2025_operating_cash_flow_capital_expenditures_free_cash_flow_capex_intensity_ratio_capex_ocf_amazon_alphabet_meta_microsoft_nvidia_apple.txt)

FY2025 cash-generation metrics for the six companies (all US$ billions; fiscal-year-end basis differs: Amazon/Alphabet/Meta = December; Microsoft = June; NVIDIA = late January; Apple = late September) [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:0,1,2,3,4,5,6]:

**Amazon** (FYE Dec): OCF $139.5B, capex $131.8B, FCF $7.7B, capex/OCF 94% [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:1]
**Alphabet** (FYE Dec): OCF $164.7B, capex $91.4B, FCF $73.3B, capex/OCF 56% [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:2]
**Meta** (FYE Dec): OCF $115.8B, capex $69.7B, FCF $46.1B, capex/OCF 60% [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:3]
**Microsoft** (FYE Jun): OCF $136.2B, capex $64.6B, FCF $71.6B, capex/OCF 47% [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:4]
**NVIDIA** (FYE Jan): OCF $64.1B, capex $3.2B, FCF $60.9B, capex/OCF 5% [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:5]
**Apple** (FYE Sep): OCF $111.5B, capex $12.7B, FCF $98.8B, capex/OCF 11% [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:6]

Capex intensity (capex/OCF) ranks Amazon highest at 94%, followed by Meta (60%), Alphabet (56%), and Microsoft (47%), while Apple (11%) and NVIDIA (5%) sit far below [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:1–6]. NVIDIA is the only company where capex intensity remained minimal despite surging revenue and OCF [doc_Analyst_Prep_Notes_-_Capex___Cash_Generation.md:2].

FCF was highest at Apple ($98.8B) and Alphabet ($73.3B), while Amazon's aggressive capex compressed FCF to just $7.7B [doc_Analyst_Prep_Notes_-_Capex___Cash_Generation.md:1,3]. These figures match the FY2025 rows in key_metrics.csv, which corroborate the same OCF, capex, FCF, and capex/OCF values for all six companies [doc_key_metrics.csv.md:5,11,16]. Definitions used throughout: FCF = Operating cash flow − Capex; Capex intensity = Capex / Operating cash flow [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:0].

### [S6] cross company comparison capex intensity operating margin free cash flow relative ranking amazon alphabet meta microsoft nvidia apple fy2025
(source: cross_company_comparison_capex_intensity_operating_margin_free_cash_flow_relative_ranking_amazon_alphabet_meta_microsoft_nvidia_apple_fy2025.txt)

Cross-Company Comparison FY2025 (figures in US$B; fiscal-year ends differ: Amazon/Alphabet/Meta=Dec, Microsoft=Jun, NVIDIA=Jan, Apple=Sep) [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:0, doc_key_metrics.csv.md:0].

**Operating margin ranking (high→low):** NVIDIA 62.4% > Microsoft 45.6% > Meta 41.4% > Alphabet 32.0% = Apple 32.0% > Amazon 11.2% [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:4,5,6; doc_Analyst_Prep_Notes_-_Capex___Cash_Generation.md:1,2,3].

**Capex intensity (Capex/OCF) ranking (low→high):** NVIDIA 5% > Apple 11% > Microsoft 47% > Alphabet 56% > Meta 60% > Amazon 94%. Absolute capex: Amazon $131.8B > Alphabet $91.4B > Meta $69.7B > Microsoft $64.6B > Apple $12.7B > NVIDIA $3.2B [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:2,3,4,5,6; doc_Analyst_Prep_Notes_-_Capex___Cash_Generation.md:1,2,3].

**Free cash flow ranking (high→low):** Apple $98.8B > Alphabet $73.3B > Microsoft $71.6B > NVIDIA $60.9B > Meta $46.1B > Amazon $7.7B [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:2,3,4,5,6; doc_Analyst_Prep_Notes_-_Capex___Cash_Generation.md:1,2,3].

NVIDIA and Apple stand out as capital-light cash machines, converting near-total OCF to FCF (Capex/OCF 5% and 11%, respectively). In contrast, Amazon consumed 94% of its OCF on capex in FY2025, compressing FCF to just $7.7B; Meta (60%) and Alphabet (56%) also redirected the majority of OCF into AI/data-center spending [doc_Analyst_Prep_Notes_-_Capex___Cash_Generation.md:1,2,3]. Microsoft's capex intensity rose to 47% but it still converted $71.6B to FCF [doc_key_metrics.csv.md:11]. Amazon reported the lowest operating margin (11.2%) yet the largest revenue ($716.9B); NVIDIA, smallest revenue base ($130.5B), achieved the highest margin (62.4%). Alphabet and Apple both posted 32.0% margins [doc_Analyst_Prep_Notes_-_Capex___Cash_Generation.md:1,2,3; doc_key_metrics.csv.md:2,5,11,16].

### [S7] capex trend 2020 2021 2022 2023 2024 fy2025 annual capital expenditures growth amazon alphabet meta microsoft nvidia apple
(source: capex_trend_2020_2021_2022_2023_2024_fy2025_annual_capital_expenditures_growth_amazon_alphabet_meta_microsoft_nvidia_apple.txt)

Tendance des dépenses d'investissement (capex) annuelles de 2020 à FY2025, par société (US$ milliards, base d'exercice fiscal propre à chaque société) :

- **Amazon** (FYE déc.) : passage de $40,1B (FY2020) à $131,8B (FY2025), avec $83,0B en FY2024 ; croissance d'environ 3,3x sur la période, capex représentant 94% du flux de trésorerie d'exploitation en FY2025 [doc_key_metrics.csv.md:0][doc_key_metrics.csv.md:2][doc_Analyst_Prep_Notes_-_Capex___Cash_Generation.md:1].
- **Alphabet** (FYE déc.) : $22,3B (FY2020) → $24,6B (FY2021) → $31,5B (FY2022) → $32,3B (FY2023) → $52,5B (FY2024) → $91,4B (FY2025), soit ~4,1x ; l'essentiel de l'accélération a lieu en FY2024-FY2025, avec une intensité capex/OCF passant de 34% à 56% [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:2].
- **Meta** (FYE déc.) : $15,2B (FY2020) → $18,7B (FY2021) → $31,2B (FY2022) → $27,0B (FY2023) → $37,3B (FY2024) → $69,7B (FY2025), soit ~4,6x [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:3].
- **Microsoft** (FYE juin) : $15,4B (FY2020) → $20,6B (FY2021) → $23,9B (FY2022) → $28,1B (FY2023) → $44,5B (FY2024) → $64,6B (FY2025), soit ~4,2x ; intensité capex/OCF en hausse de 25% à 47% [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:4][doc_key_metrics.csv.md:9].
- **NVIDIA** (FYE janv.) : capex non disponible pour FY2020 et FY2021 ; la série débute en FY2022 à $1,0B, puis $1,8B (FY2023), $1,1B (FY2024) et $3,2B (FY2025) — augmentation d'environ 3,2x sur FY2022-FY2025, avec une intensité capex très faible (5% de l'OCF) [doc_Capital-Expenditure_Reference_Data__from_SEC_10-K__1.md:5][doc_Analyst_Prep_Notes_-_Capex___Cash_Generation.md:3].
- **Apple** (FYE sept.) : $7,3B (FY2020) → $11,1B (FY2021) → $10,7B (FY2022) → $11,0B (FY2023) → $9,4B (FY2024) → $12,7B (FY2025), soit ~1,7x — la croissance la plus faible et la plus volatile du groupe [doc_key_metrics.csv.md:14][doc_key_metrics.csv.md:16][doc_Analyst_Prep_Notes_-_Capex___Cash_Generation.md:3].

**Synthèse** : sur l'ensemble du corpus (FY2020→FY2025), les capex ont fortement accéléré chez Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft et Amazon (multiplication par 3,3 à 4,6), portées par l'investissement dans l'IA/infrastructure ; NVIDIA affiche la plus forte croissance relative mais à partir d'une base très faible (FY2022), tandis qu'Apple présente la croissance la plus modeste (~1,7x). Aucune guidance FY2025 n'est disponible dans le corpus pour Microsoft, NVIDIA et Apple [doc_Initial_FY2025_Capex_Guidance_-_Frozen_as_of_Febru.md:2].
